chunks: O believers, ordained for you is retribution for the murdered, (whether) a free man (is guilty) of (the murder of) a free man, or a slave of a slave, or a woman of a woman.
But he who is parded some of it by his brother should be dealt with equity, and recompense (for blood) paid with a grace.
This is a concession from your Lord and a kindness. He who transgresses in spite of it shall suffer painful punishment.

key_terms.الْقِصَاصُ: Retaliation or retribution in kind, specifically for murder

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic law of Qisas and how does forgiveness work in cases of murder?
ai.summary: This foundational verse from Surah Al-Baqarah establishes Qisas as a divine right of the heir rather than a state-imposed penalty, allowing for proportional retribution or the acceptance of Diya (blood money). Shia scholarship emphasizes the phrase 'bi-l-ma'ruf' (with good conduct), interpreting it as a moral imperative for the heir to exercise grace and fairness when accepting compensation, thereby transforming legal justice into spiritual mercy.
